info.name: Retail Promotion Scraper
info.description:
Scrape competitor pricing and promotions.

A scrape takes 1-40 minutes, far longer than an HTTP request survives, so POST /scrape returns immediately with a job started and the work continues in the background. Poll `GET /runs/latest/{retailer_key}` until status is no longer "running".

Start the server:

    .venv/Scripts/uvicorn api:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

Set the `baseUrl` variable if it is not on localhost.

variable.description: Filled in automatically by 'Latest run' once a run has started.
Folder-name form of the retailer: boots, john_lewis, marks_and_spencer, allbeauty, asos, amazon_uk, lookfantastic, next.

request.description: Is the API up, how many runs are on disk, and which retailers are crawling right now.

The 8 adapters, what each supports, and whether it is currently running.

`supports_categories` - can honour a --categories filter.
`confirms_brand_stocking` - can tell 'not stocked' from 'we found nothing'.
`has_campaign_hubs` - campaigns_only will work.

AllBeauty is the fastest retailer (under a minute), so it is the one to test with.

`max_products` caps products PER BRAND. Omit it for a full run.

Returns 202 with a `poll` URL. It does NOT wait for the crawl.

A real run. Boots takes roughly 35 minutes.

Brand spellings are corrected automatically: "Bobbie Brown" becomes "Bobbi Brown".

Every promotion the retailer is running, regardless of brand. No brands needed.

Fast - it only reads the offers pages. M&S returns about 29 campaigns.

Every command-line flag is available.

`retailer` accepts a name, a domain or a full URL.
`categories` - only for retailers where supports_categories is true.
`strict_brand` - only accept brands proved by structured data. Fewer records, higher confidence.
`refusal_limit` - share of refused requests before the run is called failed (default 0.30).

Send this WHILE the same retailer is running.

Returns 409, not a second crawl - two browsers on one shop get both of them throttled and both come back short.

The check reads the same lock file run.py takes, so the API cannot claim something is running when it is not.

Poll this after starting a scrape. Saves the run_id into a collection variable, so the requests below just work.

`running: true`   still crawling
`status: ok`      finished, data is good
`status: failed`  finished, but do not trust it - see `reason`
`status: incomplete`  the run was killed part-way
Every run, newest first. Add `retailer` to filter.

The full record of one run: status, reason, product and campaign counts, requests made and refused, duration, brands that returned nothing, and any warnings.

This is the row worth keeping in a warehouse.
Plain text, every request the crawl made. The first place to look when a run fails.

Every product from the run. Enable `brand` to filter to one.

Each record carries: current_price, original_price, discount_percent, currency, availability, promotional_copy, applied_campaigns, and brand_verified_by - which records HOW the brand was proved.

Promotions the retailer is running.

`scope` says how widely each applies:
  sitewide   - a banner on every page
  brand      - tied to one brand
  category   - tied to a department
  product    - tied to one item
  unresolved - found it, cannot prove its reach

What the run refused to publish, and why: missing_price, brand_mismatch, discount_mismatch, unverified_brand.

Rejections are output on purpose - you can see what was refused rather than wondering why a count looks low.

Where one retailer undercuts another on the same product - the question the project exists to answer.

Uses the newest successful run of every retailer. Needs at least two.

`threshold` is title similarity, 0-1. Lower it for more matches, at the cost of pairing products that only read alike.

Check two flags before quoting a gap:
  rrp_disagreement  - the shops disagree on the RRP, so these may be different products
  currency_mismatch - not all offers were in one currency
Same thing, limited to the retailers you name. Use the folder-name form: boots, john_lewis, marks_and_spencer, allbeauty, asos, amazon_uk, lookfantastic.
